 How do I turn on the earbuds?
 First-Time Use:
1. Open the charging case.
2. Remove the insulation film from each earbud.
3. Place the earbuds back in the case and close the lid.
4. Remove the earbuds again. They will power on automatically, the charging case LED will flash rapidly, and the earbuds will enter pairing mode.
Without the Charging Case:
Press and hold both earbud buttons simultaneously for 6 seconds. Release when you hear the power-on tone.
 How do I turn off the earbuds?
 1. Place the earbuds back in the charging case to power them off automatically. The charging case indicator light will light up for about 2 seconds, then turn off.
2. If the charging case is not available, press and hold both earbuds simultaneously for 6 seconds to power them off.
 How do I connect the earbuds via Bluetooth?
 First-Time Pairing:
Open the charging case, remove the insulation film from each earbud, place the earbuds back in the case, close the lid, and then take them out again. The earbuds will automatically enter pairing mode, and a confirmation tone will play once pairing is successful. No additional steps are required.
After the first pairing is complete, the earbuds will automatically reconnect to your last-used device each time you turn them on. No manual steps are required.
Manual Pairing:
If you want to connect to a new device, pair with a second device, or the earbuds don't enter pairing mode automatically as expected, try either of the following methods:
1. Pair While Wearing the Earbuds: Press and hold both earbud buttons for 3 seconds. Release them when you hear the pairing tone. The earbuds will become discoverable. Select "ANKER AeroClip 2" from your device's Bluetooth list to complete pairing.
2. Pair via the Charging Case: Place the earbuds in the case with the lid open, then press and hold the case button for at least 3 seconds. When the indicator light flashes white rapidly, the earbuds have entered pairing mode. Search for and select "ANKER AeroClip 2" from your device's Bluetooth list to complete pairing.
 How do I wear the earbuds correctly?
 Follow these steps for a comfortable, secure fit:
1. Identify Left and Right: Before wearing, identify the left and right earbuds to ensure correct orientation.
2. Open the Bridge: Pull the flexible C-shaped bridge slightly and slide the earbud onto your ear.
3. Position the Earbud: Align the sound nozzle with the opening of your ear canal (the nozzle does not need to be inserted into the ear canal), and let the rear battery compartment rest behind your ear.
4. Adjust for Fit: Slide the earbud up or down, or gently adjust the C-shaped bridge until the earbud feels comfortable and secure.
During exercise, position the battery compartment slightly lower behind your ear for added stability.
 How do I connect the earbuds to the app for the first time?
 If you're a new user, download the latest version of the soundcore app (v4.0.1 or later) from the App Store or Google Play, then tap "Add Device" and select "ANKER AeroClip 2" to connect.
If you already have the soundcore app installed, update the app to v4.0.10 or later, then select "ANKER AeroClip 2" from the device list to connect.
If your earbuds show as connected via Bluetooth but will not connect in the soundcore app, this may occur in earlier versions of the app. Update to v4.0.10 or later via the App Store or Google Play. After updating, you should be able to connect to ANKER AeroClip 2 successfully.
 How do I connect to two devices simultaneously?
 Dual-device connection is enabled by default. You can enable or disable this feature in the soundcore app settings. You can also manage or remove connected devices from the same page.
How to Connect: Once the earbuds are paired with your first device, press and hold the left and right earbud buttons for 3 seconds to enter dual-device pairing mode. You can then search for and connect a second device.
Once dual-device connection is enabled, "Auto-Switch" is used by default. This means the earbuds will automatically switch to whichever device starts playing audio. You can also switch to "Manual Control" on the Multi-Device Connection page in the soundcore app.
 How do I turn off the low-battery alert tone?
 You can turn off the low-battery alert tone in the soundcore app.
To Turn It Off: Open the soundcore app, go to "AeroClip 2," tap Settings in the top-right corner, then tap "Low Battery Prompt" and select "Off."
Note: Currently, only the low-battery prompt tone can be turned off.
 How do I update the earbuds' firmware?
 You can update your earbuds' firmware through the soundcore app.
How to Update: Open the soundcore app, go to "AeroClip 2," navigate to "Settings," then tap "Update Firmware."
 How do I use the sound presets?
 The earbuds use the "soundcore Signature" sound preset by default. You can also select other sound profiles in the soundcore app, including soundcore Signature, Clear Vocals, Powerful Bass, Calm and Soothing, Volume Booster, Custom EQ, and Spatial Audio.
How to Access Them: Open the soundcore app, go to "AeroClip 2," then tap "HearID" and select your preferred preset.
 How is the earbud's C-shaped bridge designed?
 The earbud's C-shaped bridge is wrapped in a skin-friendly material over a 0.02" (0.45 mm) memory titanium wire structure. You can gently spread it slightly for a comfortable fit, but do not spread it more than 0.2" (5 mm) to avoid affecting its structure or fit.
 What are the default button controls?
 When Wearing Both Earbuds:
- Press either earbud once: Play / pause music.
- Press the left earbud twice: Skip to the previous track.
- Press the right earbud twice: Skip to the next track.
- Press either earbud three times: Enter / exit Nap Mode (white noise mode).
- Press and hold either earbud for 2 seconds: Unassigned by default.
When Wearing Only One Earbud:
- Press once: Play / pause music.
- Press twice: Skip to the next track.
These are the default button settings. You can customize the functions assigned to single press, double press, and press-and-hold controls in the soundcore app.
 How do I control music playback?
 While wearing the earbuds, you can control playback as follows:
When Wearing Both Earbuds:
- Press either earbud once: Play / pause music.
- Press the left earbud twice: Skip to the previous track.
- Press the right earbud twice: Skip to the next track.
- Press either earbud three times: Enter / exit Nap Mode (white noise mode).
- Press and hold either earbud for 2 seconds: Unassigned by default.
When Wearing Only One Earbud:
- Press once: Play / pause music.
- Press twice: Skip to the next track.
Notes:
1. These are the default button settings. You can customize the functions assigned to single press, double press, and press-and-hold controls in the soundcore app.
2. The controls for wearing both earbuds and wearing a single earbud are independent and do not carry over between modes. For example, if you set "Press the Left Earbud Once" to increase volume while wearing both earbuds, that setting will not apply when you switch to wearing only the left earbud (with the right earbud back in the case). You'll need to set up the button functions separately for single-earbud mode in the soundcore app.
 How do I use call control functions?
 You can control calls as follows:
1. Answer a call: Press the button on either earbud once.
2. End a call: Press the button on either earbud twice during a call.
3. Reject a call: Press the button on either earbud twice while the call is incoming.
4. Switch between calls on two devices: If your earbuds are connected to two phones at the same time and you receive an incoming call while you're already on an active call, press the button on either earbud once to put your current call on hold and answer the second call, or press the button on either earbud twice to reject the second call and continue your current call.
 How do I adjust the volume using the buttons?
 1. Volume control is not assigned to the earbud buttons by default. To adjust volume using the buttons, customize the controls in the soundcore app and assign Volume Up or Volume Down to a single press, double press, or press-and-hold action.
2. Volume control setting only works in music mode.
 How do I activate the voice assistant?
 Voice assistant activation is turned off by default. You can enable it by customizing the button controls in the soundcore app.
How to Set It Up: Open the soundcore app and go to "AeroClip 2" > "Controls" to adjust the button function settings.
 How do I reset my AeroClip 2 to factory settings?
 You can reset the earbuds to factory settings as follows:
Place the earbuds back in the charging case and keep the lid open. Press and hold the case button for more than 10 seconds until the charging case indicator flashes red three times quickly. This means the factory reset was successful.
 How do I set the auto power-off time?
 If the earbuds aren't connected to any device, they will automatically power off after 30 minutes by default. You can change this setting in the soundcore app.
How to Set It Up: Open the soundcore app, go to "AeroClip 2," tap Settings in the top-right corner, select "Auto Power-Off," and choose your preferred time.

 What are ear clip headphones?
 Ear clip earbuds are audio devices designed to hook over the outer ear with a small, flexible clip. This design keeps the earbuds securely in place without needing to insert them deep into the ear canal, making them comfortable for extended use and ideal for active lifestyles where movement is frequent. Read this article to learn more about the principles of clip-on earbuds .
 How do clip-on earphones work?
 Earbuds that clip onto the ear work by attaching to the outer ear with a flexible bridge. They house speakers that rest just outside or lightly on the ear canal, providing sound without the need for deep insertion. This design can help users remain aware of nearby sounds while enjoying music or calls.
 How do you wear clip-on earphones?
 To wear soundcore C-bridge clip-on open-ear earbuds, follow the left and right markings, place the speaker unit in front of the ear and the battery section behind it, then slide the earbud up or down until it rests comfortably and the audio port aligns with your ear canal.  Are there earbuds that don't go in the ear?
 Yes, there are earbuds that don't go in the ear, known as open-ear earbuds , earhook earbuds and clip-on earbuds. These bluetooth earbuds sit just outside the ear canal or are clipped onto the ear, allowing for a more comfortable fit and ambient sound awareness. Consequently, it is also good for long listening, working, or traveling.

However, the main aim of these earphones is usually to provide the best possible MP3 call quality by using beamforming microphones or AI-enhanced voice processing. If blocking out noise from the environment is your main concern, an in-ear ANC model would be the best choice. AeroClip 2 uses the Anker Thus™ AI Chip for call-focused voice processing, not as a claim of in-ear-style noise isolation. If environmental noise isolation is your priority, compare a sealed in-ear ANC model.
 Are clip-on earbuds sweatproof?

Therefore, they can go along with the person during workouts and also on daily outdoor trips.  Yes. Open-ear earbuds can work well for phone calls , but call clarity depends on microphone and voice-processing performance rather than the open-ear fit alone. Models like AeroFit 2 Pro use multi-mic AI call technology, while AeroClip 2 is powered by the Anker Thus™ AI Chip and is designed for clear calls in work-from-home, open-office, and city-street settings . Because open-ear designs still let ambient sound reach the listener, they do not provide the same isolation as sealed ANC earbuds .
 Do  Open‑Ear Earbuds  Leak  Sound  Even  with  ANC?
 Some sound leakage is natural with open-ear earbuds because the ear canal is not fully sealed. ANC can reduce the background noise you hear on supported models, but it does not automatically eliminate sound that other people may hear. Leakage still depends on listening volume, fit, distance, and how quiet the surrounding space is, so use a moderate volume when privacy matters.
 Which open ear earbuds are best?
 For the best open-ear earbuds , choose by how you plan to wear them. For workouts and an adjustable fit, soundcore AeroFit 2 offers 4-level adjustable ear hooks and IP55 water resistance. For quieter listening when you need it, AeroFit 2 Pro switches between open-ear and ANC modes. For all-day clip-on comfort, AeroClip and C40i clip onto the outer ear instead of hooking over it. For frequent calls, AeroClip 2 uses the Anker Thus™ AI Chip to keep your voice clear. For a lower-cost start, look at C30i, C50i, or V30i.
 Are open ear earbuds worth it?
 Absolutely! Open-ear earbuds provide a perfect balance of comfort, sound quality, and situational awareness. With secure, non-intrusive designs and advanced audio technologies, these wireless earbuds  deliver an immersive experience while keeping you connected to your surroundings. Whether for work, workouts, or daily use, they offer great value for their features.
 Are open-ear headphones good for running?
 Yes. Open-ear headphones keep the ear canal open, so traffic, footsteps, and other runners are easier to hear . For running, soundcore AeroFit 2 adds adjustable ear hooks for a secure fit, an IP55 rating for sweat and rain, and up to 10 hours of playtime per charge (42 hours with the charging case). Hearing your surroundings helps, but it does not replace following traffic rules and staying alert.
 Do open ear headphones leak sound?
 Since open-ear earbuds don’t seal the ear canal, some sound leakage is inevitable, especially at high volumes. However, soundcore’s audio engineering for adjustable open-ear and clip-on earbuds minimizes leakage while maintaining a rich, immersive sound experience. If used at moderate volume levels, they balance privacy and openness effectively.
 Which is better, open ear or bone conduction?
 Air-conduction open-ear earbuds often suit listeners who want fuller bass and treble while staying connected to their surroundings, while bone-conduction headphones send vibrations through the cheekbones and can prioritize a different type of situational awareness. The better choice depends on fit, sound preference, activity, and environment. For specific needs like hearing assistance or cycling safety, consult the relevant professional guidance and local rules rather than relying on headphone type alone.
 Do open-ear earbuds provide good sound quality?
 Yes, soundcore open-ear earbuds can deliver impressive sound quality while keeping your ears free. For example, the AeroFit 2 Pro uses a dual-mode acoustic architecture and 11.8 mm custom dual-zone composite drivers to ensure clear highs, rich mids, and punchy lows. Its adaptive EQ automatically optimizes sound depending on the earbud’s shape (open or noise-cancelling), so music, podcasts, and calls all sound balanced and detailed, even when your ears stay completely open. AeroClip 2 uses a 12 mm dual-magnetic high-excursion driver with a metal-and-polymer diaphragm for punchy bass and detailed highs.
 Are open-ear earbuds comfortable for long listening sessions?
 Yes, open-ear earbuds are generally very comfortable for extended wear since they don’t sit inside the ear canal. AeroClip, for example, clips onto the outer ear with a flexible open ring, so nothing presses into the ear canal during long bike rides , walking, or office work . Comfort still depends on ear shape, wearing position, and session length.
 Do open-ear earbuds have good battery life?
 Many open-ear earbuds offer long battery performance since they are designed for lightweight daily use. soundcore AeroFit 2 provides 10 hours of continuous playback in a single charge, 42 hours with the charging case, allowing you to enjoy music or calls throughout the day without frequent recharging.
 What is soundcore AeroClip 2 designed for?
 soundcore AeroClip 2 is an open-ear clip-on option designed around call clarity, all-day comfort, and situational awareness. It uses the Anker Thus™ AI Chip for clearer voice capture, a GoldenFit™ C-Bridge for a secure yet soft hold, and a 12 mm dual-magnetic high-excursion driver for punchy bass and detailed highs.
 Can AeroClip 2 cancel background noise like ANC earbuds?
 No. AeroClip 2 is an open-ear clip-on design, so it keeps the ear canal open and does not work like sealed ANC earbuds. The Anker Thus™ AI Chip is designed to help the other person hear your voice more clearly on calls in work-from-home, open-office, and city-street settings; it does not block the sounds you hear around you. If you need a quieter listening mode, AeroFit 2 Pro is the open-ear option on this collection with dual-mode ANC.
